mechanism_narrative: A higher level of the Consumer Price Index (CPIAUCSL) directly erodes real corporate profit margins and increases real interest rates, compressing equity valuations and resulting in negative S&P 500 forward 20-day returns regardless of economic regime.
failure_condition: SPX 20-day returns are positive in more than 60% of observations when CPIAUCSL exceeds 260, or the Rank IC over a 3-year rolling window is below 0.03.

mechanism_narrative: When the unemployment rate (UNRATE) exceeds 5.5%, it signals an economic slowdown that reduces consumer spending and corporate earnings growth expectations, leading to negative S&P 500 forward 20-day returns.
failure_condition: SPX 20-day returns are positive in more than 60% of instances when UNRATE > 5.5, or the Rank IC over a 3-year rolling window is below 0.03.

mechanism_narrative: Simultaneous expansion in labor market strength (PAYEMS > 144000) and housing market activity (HOUST > 1700) indicates robust consumer spending power, driving corporate revenue growth and producing positive S&P 500 forward 20-day returns.
failure_condition: SPX 20-day returns are negative in more than 60% of instances when PAYEMS > 144000 and HOUST > 1700, or the Rank IC over a 3-year rolling window is below 0.03.

mechanism_narrative: In a monetary tightening cycle, a decline in industrial production (INDPRO < 105) signals manufacturing sector weakness that reduces corporate earnings, resulting in negative S&P 500 forward 20-day returns.
failure_condition: SPX 20-day returns are positive in more than 60% of instances when INDPRO < 105 during a monetary tightening cycle, or the Rank IC over a 3-year rolling window is below 0.03.

mechanism_narrative: A housing market expansion (HOUST > 1800) reflects strong consumer confidence and business investment, driving sustained economic growth and positive S&P 500 forward 60-day returns.
failure_condition: SPX 60-day returns are negative in more than 60% of instances when HOUST > 1800, or the Rank IC over a 3-year rolling window is below 0.03.

mechanism_narrative: A high non-farm payrolls level (PAYEMS > 144000) indicates a tight labor market that supports consumer spending and corporate revenue growth, leading to positive S&P 500 forward 5-day returns.
failure_condition: SPX 5-day returns are negative in more than 60% of instances when PAYEMS > 144000, or the Rank IC over a 3-year rolling window is below 0.03.

mechanism_narrative: Strong quarterly GDP growth (GDPC1 > 19000) signals robust economic momentum that supports corporate earnings, resulting in positive S&P 500 forward 20-day returns.
failure_condition: SPX 20-day returns are negative in more than 60% of instances when GDPC1 > 19000, or the Rank IC over a 3-year rolling window is below 0.03.

mechanism_narrative: A federal funds rate above 0.1% indicates monetary tightening that increases borrowing costs and reduces corporate investment, leading to negative S&P 500 forward 20-day returns.
failure_condition: SPX 20-day returns are positive in more than 60% of instances when FEDFUNDS > 0.1, or the Rank IC over a 3-year rolling window is below 0.03.
